_comment: Hand-maintained ask-override list for VERIFIED upstream catalog `mutating` mislabels —
the one sanctioned exception to catalog-derived guard behavior (AGENTS.md design
tenet 6; approved by Bradley, 2026-07-11). Each entry FORCES the guard's approval
prompt on a command the catalog marks non-mutating but that was verified to write to
the tenant. Overrides can only ever ADD asks: `whileCatalogMutatingIs` must be
literally false, and any entry with another value (or a malformed entry, or a
malformed file) is ignored — the guard falls back to plain catalog behavior.
Self-retiring: an entry applies only while the catalog in use still shows `mutating`
equal to `whileCatalogMutatingIs`; once upstream fixes the flag, the entry stops
matching and the normal catalog ask takes over with no double prompt — delete the
entry at leisure. Fields per entry: `path` — the catalog command path (canonical or
short form, e.g. 'rules-engine rules run-now' or 're r run-now');
`whileCatalogMutatingIs` — always false; `unlessArgPresent` — optional flag whose
presence as an EXACT literal token exempts the invocation (the command's safe mode;
an '='-glued form like '--test-run=false' does NOT exempt — it still asks, and a
malformed value here disables only the exemption, never the ask); `reason` — shown
in the approval prompt (clamped to printable ASCII); `verifiedOnCli` — the CLI
version the mislabel was verified on: recheck the entry whenever the documented CLI
version changes.
THE LIST IS EMPTY BECAUSE UPSTREAM CLOSED THE CLASS AT CLI 1.0.8 (adopted here
2026-08-15, per the gs-fortress audit of 1.0.8). All eleven entries self-retired:
every overridden path is in that release's mutatingFlips — upstream flipped 39
commands to `mutating: true`, taking the strict non-mutating-write class
(PUT/DELETE/PATCH on a non-mutating command) from 29 to 0, with the 20 remaining
write-shaped POSTs all read-shaped (list/describe/fetch-data/validate) and reviewed
by upstream. The `mutating` flag is now a written contract in the package's
artifact.meta.schema.json: true iff the action can produce a server-side side effect
regardless of HTTP verb. The guard now asks on all eleven former entries from the
catalog itself, with the plain mutating-command prompt. KEEP this file, its schema,
and the guard's override mechanism even while empty: the schema still defaults
`mutating` to false, so a future action can ship mislabeled, and this is the
machinery that catches it (the diff-catalogs `nonMutatingWrites` tripwire is the
detection side). Retirement lesson (F-268, caught by the tester): the entries were
designed to self-retire PER WORKSPACE against the catalog in use, and deleting them
globally exposed workspaces whose .gs-superadmin/catalog.json still predated 1.0.8 -
the guard went silent on all eleven paths there. Closed structurally, not by
restoring the list: the guard now decides on the UNION of the workspace catalog and
the plugin's bundled one, so a stale workspace copy cannot silence a writer either
catalog flags. Future retirements need no version gate - the union carries corrected
labels to stale workspaces automatically.
HISTORY (the retired list and its decision record, preserved verbatim in substance):
The eleven retired entries were: re r run-now (unlessArgPresent --test-run; LIVE
verified 1.0.4/1.0.6 via PV-3), re r schedule-basic, re r schedule, re c
schedule-basic, re r schedule-event, re c schedule-event, re r schedule-s3, re c
schedule-s3, re c delete-schedule, re r delete-schedule (all endpoint-verified on the
1.0.6 scheduling surface, audited 2026-07-27), and re r set-source-template (LIVE
verified 2026-08-08 on 1.0.7 via PV-5 — the attach REPLACED an existing rule's source
graph and a re-run APPENDED a disconnected second graph; added on principled grounds,
Verification bases used (kept for future entries): LIVE — observed writing to a
sandbox tenant. ENDPOINT — read from the pinned CLI's own artifact manifests: DELETE
calls and subscribe/schedule POSTs are writes by API contract.
Deliberate non-entries, decided at 1.0.6 adoption (2026-07-28; revised the same day
by the pre-release review gate, F-088): `re r test-schedule` — POST
/v1/api/schedule/validate is validation-only (computes cron occurrences, writes
nothing). `rp run-saved` — its POST is the fetch-data call, a read-shaped fetch
RPC, not a write. Both remain catalog-non-mutating at 1.0.8, and upstream's own
review reached the same command-for-command conclusion. The wider pre-1.0.6
non-mutating-write class (re r edit, add-action/edit-action/delete-action, dd t
add-task/edit-task/delete, set-source…) stayed catalog-governed and DOCUMENTED
(plugin README write-surface callout) rather than overridden — the 0.23.x-era
decision — until upstream flipped the whole class at 1.0.8. Two class members had
earlier gained entries on principled grounds, not blanket expansion: `re r schedule`
(synonym coherence — it POSTs the identical endpoint as `re r schedule-basic`, and
ask-or-silent must not depend on which synonymous spelling an agent picks) and
`re r delete-schedule` (its endpoint set CHANGED at 1.0.6 — it gained the
event-unsubscribe DELETE). A general write-endpoint guard rule (ask whenever a
non-mutating command's endpoints contain PUT/DELETE/PATCH) was considered and
DEFERRED at 1.0.6 as a design change beyond adoption scope; it is moot at 1.0.8
with the strict class empty, and the recorded reasoning stands should the class
ever repopulate.
